steps.title: Check the parts and workspace
steps.text: Check the UNO R3 model, data cable and all listed parts. Open Arduino IDE and install Arduino AVR Boards using Boards Manager.
steps.check: Check actual parts against the guide; the inventory form is optional.
steps.safety: Use computer USB power only. Disconnect power before wiring changes. Beginners should have an experienced person check the circuit.

steps.title: Connect the circuit
steps.text: Use the onboard LED or USB communication for this example; no external wiring is needed.
steps.check: Check for shorts between 5 V and GND. Check resistor values and LED polarity where applicable.

steps.title: Upload the sketch
steps.text: Paste the code into a new sketch. Select Arduino Uno and the board’s port. Click Verify, then Upload. No additional libraries are required.
steps.check: The IDE reports a successful upload. If the port is missing, check the data cable and connection.

steps.title: Test and record
steps.text: Watch the onboard LED turn on for one second and off for one second. Time five complete cycles.
steps.check: Record your own measurements with units. Compare with the expected behaviour; do not copy example numbers as results.

steps.text: Check the UNO R3 model, data cable and all listed parts. Open Arduino IDE and install Arduino AVR Boards using Boards Manager.
steps.check: Check actual parts against the guide; the inventory form is optional.
steps.safety: Use computer USB power only. Disconnect power before wiring changes. Beginners should have an experienced person check the circuit.

steps.title: Connect the circuit
steps.text: Disconnect USB and connect the listed points. Check component pinouts against manufacturer information before applying power.
steps.check: Check for shorts between 5 V and GND. Check resistor values and LED polarity where applicable.
steps.safety: Do not connect mains power or external batteries. Never use damaged parts.

steps.title: Upload the sketch
steps.text: Paste the code into a new sketch. Select Arduino Uno and the board’s port. Click Verify, then Upload. No additional libraries are required.
steps.check: The IDE reports a successful upload. If the port is missing, check the data cable and connection.

steps.title: Test and record
steps.text: Open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud. Turn the dial quickly and slowly, observing lag and reading variation.
steps.check: Record your own measurements with units. Compare with the expected behaviour; do not copy example numbers as results.

smooth.limitations: Documentation reviewed; not AVR-compiled or physically tested. Averaging can reduce variation but adds lag; it does not guarantee greater accuracy.

straw-rocket.title: A paper rocket from a straw
straw-rocket.description: Explore fins, stability and design with a paper rocket powered by your breath.

requirements.label: Printed NASA Straw Rocket template
requirements.why: Required to build and measure the rocket described by NASA.

requirements.label: Clean personal drinking straw
requirements.why: Required to build and measure the rocket described by NASA.

requirements.label: Pencil for rolling paper
requirements.why: Required to build and measure the rocket described by NASA.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Required to build and measure the rocket described by NASA.

requirements.label: One roll of tape
requirements.why: Required to build and measure the rocket described by NASA.

requirements.label: Metric ruler or measuring tape
requirements.why: Required to build and measure the rocket described by NASA.

steps.title: Prepare the template and roll the body
steps.text: Get the printed Straw Rocket template from the NASA source. Cut out the rectangle, roll it lengthwise around a pencil and tape it into a tube.
steps.check: The tube slides over your straw without a large gap.
steps.safety: Use scissors carefully, with adult supervision for children. Use your own clean straw.

steps.title: Attach fins and close the nose
steps.text: Cut out both fin units and tape them to opposite sides with lower edges aligned. Fold the triangles out 90 degrees to make a + from behind. Twist the paper above the pencil tip into a nose and tape it closed.
steps.check: Fins are secure and the nose is airtight. Do not add hard or pointed parts.

steps.title: Measure and launch
steps.text: Measure the nose length and record it. Replace the pencil with the straw. Mark a starting point in a clear area, then blow the paper rocket off the straw.
steps.check: Measure the actual landing distance in cm or m.
steps.safety: Never aim at people, animals or faces. Use breath only; no pumps, pressure tanks or hard payloads.

steps.title: Change one thing at a time
steps.text: Change body length or fin shape, size or angle one at a time. Repeat from the same point and record every attempt, including failures.
steps.check: Keep designs and measurements separate. One attempt is not enough to establish which design is better.

learning: Changing one variable at a time
straw-rocket.limitations: Reviewed from NASA documentation, not physically tested. Requires a printed template from the source. No fuel or compressed-air system.

test.name: Rocket distance
test.instruction: Mark the start, clear the launch area and record each actual distance. Change only one design variable at a time.
